description.narrative:
The proposed project follows the Asian Development Bank's (ADB's) COVID-19 emergency assistance and vaccine projects in the Kyrgyz Republic and ongoing regional support. 1 It will be part of a continuum of support to health sector building on good relations and policy dialogue built over the years. It contributes to regional health security (RHS) by improving health sector resilience to outbreaks of emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases in the country. The project addresses critical bottlenecks in RHS and the country's International Health Regulations (IHR) compliance, namely diagnostic capacities and regional linkages of laboratories, and hospitals in busy border zones.
The project is aligned with the following impact: improved public health and regional health security in the Kyrgyz Republic.2 The project outcome is enhanced coverage of effective laboratory and border hospital services in Chui and Osh oblasts.

Number of essential clinical diagnostic tests including tests for female-specific health conditions, performed by project CDLs increased by at least 30% Progress/Status: Not started yet Data Source: Laboratories' baseline and end-line surveys using a standard checklist; reports generated from LIMS Actual value:

Border hospitals and points of entry capacities increased to 65% Progress/Status: From 2022 to 2024, the capacity for these facilities has improved to 60% based on the latest e-SPAR assessments. Key activities influencing this indicator: Infrastructure improvements are being implemented at 5 project-supported border hospitals. This includes renovation works (upgrades to water supply, electricity, and ventilation systems), which are essential to increasing hospital capacity. Procurement of medical equipment (including diagnostics and imaging devices) and visualization equipment (G-03) is ongoing. This equipment will directly contribute to improved hospital service delivery and the capacity of border health facilities. Training for hospital staff is a critical component in improving service delivery at border hospitals. Data Source: e-SPAR self-assessment reports; WHO laboratories' annual reports Actual value:

Public health laboratory services' capacity increased to 70% Progress/Status: Ongoing activities to drive capacity improvements include: Infrastructure upgrades in 17 laboratories (renovations, new ventilation, water and power systems). Procurement and installation of modern laboratory equipment (biochemistry, hematology, microbiology, immunochemistry). LIMS deployment Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) processes ISO 15189 accreditation readiness activities Data Source: e-SPAR self-assessment reports; WHO laboratories' annual reports Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity, quality, and networking of reference laboratories in Bishkek and Osh cities strengthened Indicator: By October 2026, four project reference laboratories are linked to peripheral laboratories through LIMS and sample-transportation services Progress/Status: b. Ongoing. The LIMS procurement process has started and proposal evaluation is underway. LIMS will connect reference and peripheral laboratories for real-time data sharing and sample tracking. Due to the 1.5-year project delay, the October 2026 target is not feasible; the timeline should be extended to October 2027 to complete LIMS installation and establish sample transportation services after equipment delivery. Data Source: Reference laboratories' baseline and end-line surveys Actual value:

Output: Capacity, quality, and networking of reference laboratories in Bishkek and Osh cities strengthened Indicator: By October 2026, four project reference laboratories have applied for ISO 15189 accreditation Progress/Status: a. Ongoing. A working group on ISO 15189 was established, and a roadmap for four reference laboratories is being developed. CQI consultancy procurement is in progress. Due to the project's late start, submission for ISO 15189 accreditation is not feasible by October 2026; the target should be shifted to October 2027. Upcoming steps include gap analysis, capacity building, and LIMS procurement to support ISO 15189 compliance. Data Source: Reference laboratories' baseline and end-line surveys. Reference laboratories' annual reports; project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity, quality, and networking of reference laboratories in Bishkek and Osh cities strengthened Indicator: By September 2028, at least 75% of project reference laboratories (national and subnational) accredited to an international ISO laboratory standard Progress/Status: e. Ongoing. A Working Group on ISO 15189 compliance was established in January 2025. The CQI consultancy (CS-04) ToR has been submitted to ADB, and proposal evaluation is in progress. Gap analyses for ISO 15189 compliance have started. Data Source: Reference laboratories' baseline and end-line surveys. Reference laboratories' annual reports; project progress reports. Actual value:

Output: Laboratory services based on continuous quality improvement in Chui and Osh oblasts (including Bishkek and Osh cities) developed Indicator: At least 70% of 13 non-reference project laboratories meet national quality and safety standards Progress/Status: b. Ongoing. In 2022 ISO 15189 has been formally adopted as the national standard and now serves as the benchmark for quality and safety in laboratories. CQI consultancy will support laboratories in meeting these standards, including gender-sensitive workplace measures. Ongoing renovations and procurement of laboratory equipment will help ensure compliance with safety and quality requirements and contribute to achieving the 70% target by September 2028. Data Source: Chui and Osh laboratories' baseline and end-line surveys. Chui and Osh laboratories' annual reports; project progress reports. Annual monitoring using standard checklist.
Actual value:

Output: Patient care and biosafety capacity in hospitals in border areas and high travel zones in Chui and Osh oblasts improved Indicator: By April 2026, six border hospitals upgraded with low carbon and climate-resilient infrastructure and equipment for improved patient and provider care and surge capacity Progress/Status: a. Ongoing. Although renovations were initially planned for all six hospitals, one declined as upgrades are being financed from other sources. Thus, five hospitals will receive infrastructure modernization, while all six will receive medical and climate-resilient equipment. Civil works have been completed at three hospital sites, works have started at one site, and bidding procedures are underway for the remaining site. Completion is planned by the end of 2026. Delays have been caused by re-bidding procedures due to various reasons. Data Source: Project quarterly progress reports using the checklist. Actual value:

Output: Laboratory services based on continuous quality improvement in Chui and Osh oblasts (including Bishkek and Osh cities) developed Indicator: Turnaround time for bacteriology culture and antimicrobial sensitivity tests decreased to 3 days Progress/Status: d. Ongoing. Procurement of microbiology analyzers and rapid AST platforms (G-01/4) has been completed, and the supply contract is signed. Installation of these platforms will substantially reduce culture and sensitivity turnaround times. The CQI consultancy (CS-04) ToR includes process mapping of bacteriology workflows to identify and address delays. Data Source: Chui and Osh laboratories' baseline and end-line surveys. Chui and Osh laboratories' annual reports; project progress reports. Annual monitoring using standard checklist. Reports generated from LIMS. Actual value:

Output: Capacity, quality, and networking of reference laboratories in Bishkek and Osh cities strengthened Indicator: By September 2028, each project reference laboratory participates in external quality assessment for at least 50% of tests it offers, including at least 50% of tests for female-specific health conditions Progress/Status: d. Ongoing. Discussions with EQA providers have begun, and preliminary negotiations are underway. The CQI consultancy (CS-04) will support EQA integration and build laboratory capacity to meet external quality assessment standards. Data Source: Reference laboratories' baseline and end-line surveys. Reference laboratories' annual reports; project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Laboratory services based on continuous quality improvement in Chui and Osh oblasts (including Bishkek and Osh cities) developed Indicator: LAT score of 13 non-reference project laboratories improved to at least 70% Progress/Status: a. A working group is established, CQI and ISO 15189 activities are underway, and infrastructure upgrades (renovations, equipment, LIMS) are expected to significantly improve LAT scores by endline.
